key_insight: Simulated quantum layers can improve vision-language accuracy or reduce trainable parameters, but benefits depend strongly on placement.
engineering_relevance: For hybrid VLM design, layer placement matters: parameter savings do not reliably translate into lower computation or shorter training.
method: Used LLaVA-OneVision with classically simulated 4- and 8-qubit basic-ring and strongly entangling circuits.
Compared four quantum-layer insertion locations and four classical-component replacement locations.
Evaluated accuracy, computational cost, and robustness under six attack settings.
evidence_signal: On Visual Spatial Reasoning development data, insertion after the visual projector achieved 80.7% accuracy (+2.28 percentage points over classical full fine-tuning), while replacing the final decoder feed-forward sublayer retained 79.22% accuracy with 13.07 million fewer trainable parameters.
watch_item: Results from classical simulation do not establish quantum-hardware advantages, broader generalization, or security gains.
paper_title: Can Quantum Layers offer Performance and Security Advantages in Vision-Language Models?
